parallel.requirements: Recognized the base58/test14.py requirements: required --a and --b ints, required --c string, base58 integer encode/decode, Python print/bytes formatting, ESM .mjs modules, no npm dependencies, no Python calls, and /output delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and integration, then launched a workflow that split verification into fuzz categories, audit lenses, verification of reported issues, and synthesis.
parallel.implementation: Built a hierarchical ESM implementation with Python-like Unicode/int/repr/bytes/stdio/traceback helpers, argparse behavior, base58 modules, and test14.mjs; later patched argparse, int digit limits, stream handling, and traceback behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the helper modules into /output/test14.mjs and supporting /output/lib modules. Artifact status marked the expected entry and supporting files present and ok.
parallel.verification: Used reference probes, a differential harness, broad child fuzz/audit verification, local regression sweeps, and the official evaluator; child verification included re-runs after live-target drift.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow state was killed with several child fuzzers in progress and final.txt was empty, but the current completed official evaluation passed all 131 samples.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same required flags, base58 behavior, exact Python-like output, ESM .mjs module structure, no external dependencies, no Python calls, and /output artifact placement.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept probing, implementation, integration, diff-test construction, and follow-up verification in one parent trajectory with no subagents or workflow delegation.
serial.implementation: Built local ESM modules under /output/lib/py and /output/lib/base58 plus /output/test14.mjs, including argparse, unicode/int behavior, byte repr, tracebacks, and base58 integer logic.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Assembled /output/test14.mjs with local modules and produced an artifact set accepted by the runner as artifact_ok true.
serial.verification: Ran many direct reference probes and a local tools/diff-test.mjs harness, then investigated traceback/source-line behavior; the official evaluator later passed all 131 samples.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial agent also timed out with an empty final.txt and had local harness mismatches, but the delivered artifact passed the official current evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required argparse flags, base58 encode/decode behavior, byte-string style output, ESM-only .mjs structure, no external dependencies, /output placement, and prohibited APIs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same base58 CLI, manual argument parsing, ESM module split, exact output, and dependency/API constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference remained at evaluation; both implemented the same required behavior and passed the same official suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent retained implementation ownership and used a workflow to decompose verification into fuzz, audit, verify, and synthesize phases across child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had one owner for probing, module writing, entry-point assembly, and local diff testing, with protocol validation showing no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed verification while serial kept all work in one trajectory; neither split left implementation, integration, or assembly unowned.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow briefs gave children the target file layout, the reference executable, scratch-directory expectations, and a no-edit contract for /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial preserved context locally while writing Python-semantics helpers, argparse, base58 modules, and a local diff-test tool.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit child testing briefs but no immutable snapshot boundary for their target; serial had no handoff boundary and therefore no stale or incomplete child context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a larger module tree with Python-like Unicode, int, bytes, repr, stdio, traceback, argparse, and base58 modules, then patched several edge cases found by verifiers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a comparable hierarchical implementation under /output/lib/py and /output/lib/base58 plus the test14.mjs entry point and a diff-test helper.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on a passing ESM port; parallel made more late edge-case edits during verifier execution, while serial made those probes and edits sequentially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received several completed fuzzer/verifier results through the workflow journal and state, but the aggregate workflow was killed with several children still in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it ran its own local diff-test and follow-up traceback probes directly in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had partially completed workflow results and unfinished child work; serial had only sequential local command results. This did not create an official outcome gap.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children tested the shared /output tree while the parent continued editing it, so multiple verifiers saw mutable target artifacts and checksum drift.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and tested within a single actor, with protocol validation confirming no child agents or delegated parallel work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main adverse process difference is shared-environment contamination in parallel verification; serial had no concurrent consumer of a moving implementation tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used reference probes, local differential sweeps, broad child fuzzers/auditors, and official evaluation; child verification sometimes had to be repeated because the target moved.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used reference probes and a local tools/diff-test.mjs harness; the official evaluator also completed successfully.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was broader but noisier due to live-target drift. Serial verification was narrower and sequential, but both final official evaluations passed 131/131.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed large workflow budget, the workflow state ended killed, and final.txt was empty, but artifact_ok and official evaluation still succeeded.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out with empty final.txt, but used no workflow tokens and still delivered a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more budget on child verification and suffered workflow kill/no final prose, but there was no official solution-quality difference because both artifacts passed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations are concordant: both the parallel and serial artifacts passed 131 of 131 samples with solution_passed true. The difference is therefore process-level, not an outcome cause. Parallel used child workflow verification that became noisy because children tested /output while it changed; serial performed sequential local probing and testing without child target drift.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation plus broad workflow verification produced a passing artifact, while live-target verification contamination added rework but no final failure.
serial_contributors: Single-actor probing, implementation, and local diff testing also produced a passing artifact without shared verification-state contamination.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial local diff-test output still showed mismatches before timeout, but official evaluation passed; those harness-local differences did not create a solution outcome gap.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; retained pattern describes adverse parallel process consequence only.

candidates.reason: The parallel parent owned and wrote the required implementation files before and during the verifier workflow.
The parent integrated the argparse, Python-semantics, and base58 modules into the entry point instead of leaving component integration unowned.
The parent assembled the required /output/test14.mjs entry point and supporting modules, and artifact extraction succeeded.
The parent controlled the end-to-end implementation, testing, fixes, and artifact placement pipeline despite workflow verification noise.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent probed, wrote modules, and then launched verification.
The workflow was a verification fan-out after implementation work had already begun, not an investigation-only first phase that deferred productive work.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; the parent continued the critical path and the final artifact passed.
The broad workflow was killed and consumed budget, but no required implementation, integration, or delivery work was left undone by fan-out; both modes timed out after passing artifacts existed.
No single child was assigned indispensable implementation work whose oversized scope left the task unfinished; children were verification/audit workers.

The verifier briefs included the target files, reference executable, scratch-directory rule, no-edit rule, and reporting expectations; no already-known task requirement was omitted and followed to harmful effect.
No separately owned implementation components had to interoperate without an interface contract; children were testing/auditing a parent-owned integrated tree.
No known finding disappeared in transfer; returned child results and journal entries were available or explicitly reflected their limits.
The completed child reports were lengthy but decision-structured and used or superseded; no needed returned information was left unconsumed because of bulk.
Some child observations became stale because /output moved, but children recognized the drift and re-ran or qualified results rather than the parent blindly consuming a stale handoff.
There were no unadjudicated incompatible child reports that blocked or corrupted integration; conflicting transient findings were traced to live target drift.
The parent did not make a whole-task acceptance decision unsupported by visible integrated evidence; official evaluation later passed and status evidence is not a basis for this label.
No replacement or retry child was launched without inherited findings and then repeated the same failed work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The workflow ended killed at run timeout, but no needed child result was explicitly stopped by the parent before indispensable work could be used.
A complete deliverable had already been placed in /output and artifact extraction succeeded; there was no ready candidate that missed promotion.
The parent kept re-testing after edits, and the retained episode is verifier consumption of a moving target rather than a post-verification merge without a closing check.
No child produced a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or integrate; implementation ownership stayed with the parent.
Some workflow agents remained in progress when killed, but no concrete completed verifier finding was trapped below the parent and needed for task success.
Cancelled or incomplete verifier work was not a required implementation stage; the parent continued local fixes and the artifact passed.
The parent inspected workflow progress and journaled verifier outputs, using several findings to drive fixes rather than ignoring completed results.
The parent actively polled the workflow and ran local tests, so the terminal timeout was not caused by waiting without inspecting available progress.
Children did not create competing cross-file implementations; they tested and audited a parent-owned output tree.
No child edit to the same source file is evidenced; the observed same-file changes were parent edits seen by child verifiers.
No agent replaced source produced or actively owned by another implementation agent; parent rewrites were within its own owned implementation.
No child replaced the submitted entry point while another actor owned or used it; the issue was testing a mutable deliverable, not overwriting it.
There was no broad cleanup or promotion replacing another agent's final tree; final artifact provenance remained parent-owned.

The closest concurrent-write label is not retained because multiple live agents writing /output is not shown; the concrete event was child verification consuming parent-written artifacts while they changed.

The workflow delegated verification of /output while the parent continued editing that generated implementation tree; children consumed it as a stable target and had to discard race failures, re-run, and wait for checksums to settle.
candidates.realized_consequence: Transient false failures, checksum drift, repeated re-runs, and stability waits contaminated parallel verification, though the final official artifact still passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: No child writer to /output is evidenced, so the nearest concurrent-write label is wrong; the concrete boundary is child consumption of mutable parent-generated artifacts as reference input.
